opex.name: Operating, selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Running the stores, the supply chain and the back office — includes a $0.7B one-time stock charge at PhonePe.

follow100Note: Walmart kept $3.42 of every $100 — more than usual, because paper gains on investment stakes added $1.16 of it. The stores' own slice was thinner after the one-time PhonePe charge.
footerNote: Net profit shown is the $6,143M attributable to Walmart; consolidated net income was $6,088M, after a $55M loss attributable to noncontrolling interests.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: adjusted $0.62, which strips out the investment gain

oneTimers: Other (gains) and losses was a $2,081M gain — mostly fair-value moves on equity investments (a year ago it was a $132M loss). Adjusted EPS of $0.62 excludes a $0.20-per-share net-of-tax gain from these items.

A roughly $0.7B non-cash share-based compensation charge at PhonePe (India) sits inside operating expenses, ahead of a potential PhonePe IPO — it is why reported operating income fell 0.2% while the adjusted figure rose 8.0% in constant currency.
otherDetail: A $2,081M gain on equity and other investments, less $591M of net interest expense. Noncontrolling interests absorbed a $55M loss, which is added back to reach profit attributable to Walmart.

segments.name: Walmart U.S.
segments.note: The big U.S. stores — net sales up 5.1%, comparable sales up 4.5%, with strength across categories.

segments.name: Walmart International
segments.note: Stores and e-commerce outside the U.S., including Flipkart in India — growth led by China, Walmex and Flipkart.

segments.name: Sam's Club U.S.
segments.note: The warehouse-club business — net sales up 3.1%.

segments.name: Membership & other income
segments.note: Sam's Club membership fees plus advertising — membership income itself grew 16.7%.

takeaways.text: Global eCommerce grew 27%, with every segment up more than 20%, led by store-fulfilled pickup and delivery and the marketplace. U.S. comparable sales rose 4.5% — and Walmart raised its full-year sales and profit outlook on the strength of the quarter.
takeaways.title: Online sales keep compounding

takeaways.text: International operating income fell 41.7% to $702M because of a roughly $0.7B non-cash stock-compensation charge at PhonePe, Walmart's Indian payments business, ahead of a potential IPO. Adjusted for it and currency, group operating income rose 8.0%.
takeaways.title: A one-time charge at PhonePe

takeaways.text: A $2,081M gain on equity and other investments turned a flat operating quarter into a 34% rise in headline profit, to $6.1B. Adjusted EPS of $0.62 — which strips the gain out — is the cleaner read on the stores.
takeaways.title: Paper gains lifted the headline

verdict: Walmart's revenue rose 5.8% to $179.5B and its U.S. stores earned 6.3% more — but a $0.7B one-time stock charge at PhonePe held reported operating profit flat, while a $2.1B investment gain lifted headline profit 34% to $6.1B.
